tasks.question: How does the algorithm classification system categorize and select minimization algorithms across different fitting software controllers in the benchmarking framework?
tasks.reference_answer: Controllers map named algorithm categories to minimizer lists, allowing overlap (fitbenchmarking/controllers/base_controller.py:28-63). validate_minimizer accepts membership in any requested category, while cost functions reject incompatible categories and bounds checks reject unsupported minimizers (fitbenchmarking/controllers/base_controller.py:280-310,329-343; fitbenchmarking/cost_func/base_cost_func.py:112-130). record_alg_type reports matching categories restricted to those requested, not all categories (fitbenchmarking/controllers/base_controller.py:312-327).

tasks.question: Why does the runtime metric aggregation system in fitbenchmarking use simple averaging instead of more robust statistical measures for processing multiple timing measurements?
tasks.reference_answer: perform_fit repeats one execution num_runs times, computes sum(runtime_list)/num_runs, and warns when max/min exceeds four (fitbenchmarking/core/fitting_benchmarking.py:549-575). The warning mentions caching or unrelated CPU activity and does not alter the mean. This establishes the chosen aggregation, but not why robust alternatives were rejected; claims about API simplicity or typical convergence behavior are interpretations, not demonstrated design rationale.

tasks.question: What is the algorithm categorization scheme used by the controller system to classify optimization minimizers?
tasks.reference_answer: The base algorithm_check dictionary defines all, ls, deriv_free, general, simplex, trust_region, levenberg-marquardt, gauss_newton, bfgs, conjugate_gradient, steepest_descent and global_optimization (fitbenchmarking/controllers/base_controller.py:28-63). Concrete controllers fill lists, with a minimizer eligible for multiple categories (fitbenchmarking/controllers/scipy_controller.py:17-31). validate_minimizer accepts any selected category match; record_alg_type joins only matching selected categories (fitbenchmarking/controllers/base_controller.py:280-327).

tasks.question: How does the benchmarking framework implement cross-platform execution coordination and resource cleanup in its nested benchmark pipeline?
tasks.reference_answer: OutputGrabber enables stdout/stderr capture outside Windows/debug/IPython and stops active grabbers on context exit (fitbenchmarking/utils/output_grabber.py:24-47). perform_fit validates and times controller executions inside that context; cleanup is called only after successful timing. It catches validation/general exceptions to set flags, then calls optional clear_matlab and resets the timer (fitbenchmarking/core/fitting_benchmarking.py:550-611). Thus stream restoration uses context exit, but general controller cleanup is not guaranteed after earlier failure and the later cleanup sequence is not protected by finally.
